questions.text: What is the safest Philippine-practice conclusion when a foreign architect has ASEAN or APEC registry status?

options.text: Registry status automatically creates Philippine practice authority
Registry status does not by itself replace the RA 9266 temporary or special permit and Filipino counterpart checks
Registry status makes the architect the Philippine AOR
Registry status removes all local law requirements

questions.rationale: The local sources treat registry status as application information while RA 9266 and PRBoA permit requirements still control practice authority.
questions.explanation: Misnames the organization—the correct body is AMCASP, not a general Professional Services Board. Confuses national coordination with MRA-specific oversight—the Philippine Architects Council is not the MRA implementation body. Attributes MRA oversight to a BOA division—AMCASP is the specific body, not a BOA internal division. The ASEAN Monitoring Committee on Architectural Services (AMCASP) was created in the Philippines to serve the Monitoring Committee functions under the MRA. The AMCASP oversees MRA implementation in the Philippines—it reviews ASEAN Architect conduct and reports to the international AAC.
questions.code_citation: 2007 ASEAN MRA on Architectural Services, Appendix B (ASEAN Architects Guidelines)

questions.text: What does the PRBoA temporary-permit application ask about ASEAN or APEC status?

options.text: Whether the applicant wants to skip the permit process
Whether the applicant has ASEAN or APEC registry status
Whether the applicant wants to replace the Filipino counterpart
Whether the applicant is exempt from Philippine law

questions.rationale: The source-backed point is that the form asks about registry status as information in the permit file.
questions.explanation: Falsely assumes all ASEAN architects qualify—only those meeting specific MRA requirements and registered in the AAR are ASEAN Architects. Confuses employment with credentials—institutional affiliation is irrelevant; professional certification matters. Mistakes education for status—graduation from ASEAN schools does not confer ASEAN Architect status; PRA certification and AAR registration do. An ASEAN Architect is an architect certified by their country's Professional Regulatory Authority and registered in the ASEAN Architect Register meeting all MRA requirements. ASEAN Architect status requires PRA certification from home country AND registration in the ASEAN Architect Register—not all ASEAN architects qualify.
questions.code_citation: 2007 ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement on Architectural Services

questions.text: If the ASEAN or APEC registry answer is no, what does the checked PRBoA form indicate?

options.text: The application is automatically void
The application may still proceed through the permit process

The Filipino counterpart is no longer needed

questions.rationale: The form note permits proceeding even with a no answer, so registry status is not the entire gate.

options.text: A regional credential alone
RA 9266 Section 38 temporary or special permit before duties are assumed

questions.rationale: RA 9266 Section 38 is the local practice gate for foreign nationals performing architectural services as architects or consultants.

options.text: The foreign architect automatically becomes AOR
The foreign architect may consult within permit limits, but the Filipino counterpart remains architect of record

questions.text: What is the main exam trap in ASEAN MRA practice questions?

options.text: Checking the foreign architect's role
Confusing recognition of qualifications with permission to bypass Philippine practice gates
Checking whether a Filipino counterpart exists
Checking permit timing

questions.rationale: Recognition language does not cancel the RA 9266 and PRBoA practice pathway for Philippine projects.
questions.explanation: Underestimates the MRA timeline—the arrangement was signed seven years after 2000. Misestimates the date—the MRA was signed three years after 2004. Overestimates the date—the MRA was established five years before 2012. The ASEAN MRA on Architectural Services was signed by ASEAN Economic Ministers on 20 November 2007. The ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement was adopted in 2007 to facilitate architect mobility across Southeast Asia.
questions.code_citation: 2007 ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement on Architectural Services

questions.text: Which answer is source-safe for an ASEAN architect invited to a Manila project?

options.text: The architect may sign and seal because ASEAN status exists
The architect must still satisfy the Philippine temporary-permit and counterpart framework before practice duties
The architect may ignore PRBoA permit procedure
The architect may practice without any Filipino counterpart

questions.rationale: The Philippine project remains governed by the local foreign-architect gate.
questions.code_citation: 2007 ASEAN MRA on Architectural Services, Appendix B (ASEAN Architects Guidelines)

questions.text: What evidence can the Board evaluate when no bilateral agreement is shown?

options.text: Only a project brochure
Documentary proof that Filipino architects may practice without limitation in the foreign jurisdiction
Only a client recommendation
Only the foreign firm profile

questions.rationale: The PRBoA source calls for documentary proof for Board evaluation when a bilateral agreement is absent.
questions.explanation: Overstates MRA reach—mutual recognition is not elimination; national procedures remain. Creates false carve-out—national requirements apply equally to all foreign architects, ASEAN or not. Grants false exemption—ASEAN status facilitates, not exempts, from national procedures. The MRA recognizes mutual equivalency of qualifications but does not eliminate national licensing requirements; ASEAN professionals must still comply with host country procedures. The ASEAN MRA harmonizes standards but does not replace national licensing—ASEAN Architects still must comply with host country procedures.
questions.code_citation: 2007 ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement on Architectural Services

As a private contract term

questions.rationale: RA 9266 and PRBoA sources keep reciprocity and permit authority as local legal checks.
